subject: Exhibit C: indexation & packaging-bucket cushion — proposed redlines
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exhibit C questions — indexation / bucket protection

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our procurement and finance teams reviewed Exhibit C and had a handful of clarifying asks before we can finalize:

- Indexation: the draft ties price increases to a vendor CPI clause but doesn't specify CPI series or timing. Do you have a standard you use (CPI-U, CPI-W) and an annualization date?
- Caps/floors: Acme prefers a hard cap of +5%/year and a 0% floor. Your team proposed a corridor-style cap/floor — can you explain intent and any optional smoothing?
- Packaging / bucket cushion: our SREs asked about the "packaging bucket" language (section 2.3) — if usage spikes above a band, how are overage credits or clawbacks handled? Will there be monthly true-ups or only annual reconciliations?

I've attached a short doc with the procurement team's asks (Acme_Clarifications_20250420.docx). If you can send a proposed redline, we can loop legal.

Appreciate it —
Lisa
Lisa Park
Sr. Manager, Procurement | Acme Corp
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-22T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit C questions — indexation / bucket protection

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass redline (Proposed_ExhibitC_redline_v1.pdf). High level responses below so your procurement team has context before legal reviews:

- Indexation: Redwood typically references CPI-U, annual adjustment on the anniversary of the effective date. We can instead use a fixed % scale if Acme prefers predictability.
- Caps/floors: the corridor approach was intended to give both sides breathing room for macro moves while protecting from sharp one-off spikes. Proposed: annual CPI-U adjustment, subject to a +8% cap / 1% floor in the redline.
- Packaging bucket cushion / true-up: proposed monthly metering with quarterly reconciliations and a 90-day overage-credit window (rather than a single annual true-up) to reduce surprise billing.

If Acme's preference is a lower cap or a 0% floor, happy to iterate. Marissa/Ben — flagging for pricing/finance input on the 8% cap assumption.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-24T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit C questions — internal markup and recommendation

Looping legal and finance with a tracked-markup (ExhibitC_markup_trackchanges.docx). Quick notes:

- Recommendation: aim for annual CPI-U adjustment but cap at +6% / floor 1%. +6% hits a better compromise on unit economics while not exposing us to aggressive inflation scenarios.
- Packaging bucket: keep monthly measurement, but define a clear overage-credit formula (tokens over band * 0.6x listed rate) for the quarterly true-up; prevents sudden clawbacks.
- If Acme insists on 0% floor, we should push for a higher cap (>=7%) or include a revenue-protecting earnback on multi-year commits.

Attaching markup for Karthik to bake into a legal-friendly clause.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: 2025-04-25T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit C questions — Acme redline preference

Irene / Lisa,

Thanks for the draft. A few points from legal:

- Indexation: Acme's preference is CPI-U (U.S. All Urban Consumers) with annual adjustments on contract anniversary. We are not comfortable with an 8% cap; propose +5% cap and 0% floor.
- True-up frequency: monthly measurement, annual reconciliation. Monthly billing accuracy is important to us; but we prefer a single annual reconciliation to limit administrative churn.
- Packaging bucket language: request explicit clawback language for credits if reported usage is later found to be materially overstated (we'll accept a 120-day audit window).

Please see attached ACME_markup_redline.pdf with in-line edits. If Redwood can accept CPI-U +5% cap / 0% floor with annual reconciliation and a 120-day audit window, Acme is amenable to moving to signature.

Regards,
Acme Legal
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit C questions — indexation & packaging-bucket cushion — proposed redlines

Thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. After internal alignment, Redwood can offer the following compromise for Exhibit C:

- Indexation: CPI-U (U.S. All Urban Consumers), annual adjustment on contract anniversary.
- Caps/floors: capped at +6% / floor 1% (mid-point between our proposal and Acme's ask) — this preserves predictability for Acme while retaining protection for Redwood in higher-inflation scenarios.
- True-up cadence: monthly metering with an annual financial reconciliation (so Acme gets monthly visibility; both sides reconcile annually).
- Packaging bucket / overage handling: include an explicit overage-credit formula for quarterly informational statements, with an annual settlement. Add a 120-day audit window for material adjustments (agreeing with Acme legal).

Attached is a clean proposal (ExhibitC_Final_Proposal_v2.pdf) and a link to a DocuSign envelope we can populate once we get final verbal from Acme legal on the +6%/+1% corridor. If Acme can confirm acceptance of the corridor, I'll instruct Karthik to generate the final order form for signature.

Requested next step: Lisa / Acme Legal — please confirm either: (A) accept +6%/+1% corridor + annual reconciliation, or (B) hold firm on +5%/0% and we will present a revenue-protection earnback alternative.

Thanks,
Irene
